url.h:169 -> src/common/url_mod.rs:258: for i in 0..n { y = *ptr++ } then return strdup(ptr) (line 273). Rust models ptr++ by setting ptr=None after the first iteration (267), so for n>0 it returns None instead of the suffix; structure (n-iteration loop + strdup of the advanced pointer) is the C body.

url.h:179 -> src/common/url_mod.rs:275: for i in 0..n { y = *ptr-- } then strdup(ptr) (line 297). Rust reads *p into y (286) and leaves ptr unchanged (cannot decrement a reference) — same loop + strdup structure as C; distinguishable from strff by the read-of-*p vs pointer-to-int cast and the 'decrement' comment.
